- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–5% in subsequent 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model often underreacts; increase forecast slightly to avoid underestimating mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overconfidence.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” cycles, model often misjudges mean reversion; apply smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% in mid-horizon.
